scope: 全局
diagnosis: 定位结论: 息屏/休眠后无法恢复的高风险点是 layered window 复用的 native memory DC/HBITMAP 可能跨显示驱动或 DWM 恢复后失效，而原恢复路径只将托管 Bitmap 标记为需要重绘；另一个风险是 `--desktop-parent` 模式下旧 WorkerW 父窗口失效后没有先脱离旧父窗口再重新挂接。
method: 修正内容: `NativeMethods.LayeredBitmapSurface` 增加 Reset，恢复时释放并重建 native DC/HBITMAP；主窗口、CodexRadar、功耗、网络、连接检测均在恢复时重建托管渲染缓存并重置 native surface，操作面板重建托管 Bitmap 并恢复失败日志状态。
修正内容: 屏幕关闭或系统挂起时主动释放主窗口和子窗口显示资源；显示恢复改为三轮延迟恢复，覆盖 DWM、显示驱动和 WorkerW 稍晚恢复的情况。
修正内容: `--desktop-parent` 恢复时先 `SetParent(..., IntPtr.Zero)` 脱离旧桌面宿主，恢复普通顶层窗口样式，再尝试挂接新的桌面宿主；后续恢复轮继续重试挂接。
修正内容: 新增 `--test-display-recovery`，使用真实 layered-window API 验证 native surface reset 前后均可更新窗口。

diagnosis: Claude 检测已使用官方 `https://status.claude.com/api/v2/status.json`；2026-06-15 检查时接口返回 HTTP 200、`indicator=minor`、`Partially Degraded Service`。解析层正确映射为 `Degraded`，但绘制层错误地将 `Degraded` 与断网状态一起显示为灰色叉。

同步更新服务健康状态文档、Claude 状态 API 索引和版本至 1.0.2.63。

scope: 左下角操作面板
module: 隐藏模式鼠标命中遮罩
diagnosis: 用户在正式 1.0.2.64 中仍能复现隐藏模式图标区域鼠标穿透；进程检查确认当时运行的是最新正式版本，PID 57648，FileVersion/ProductVersion 均为 1.0.2.64。
1.0.2.64 的命中遮罩只把最终透明像素恢复为 Alpha=1，而操作面板隐藏态还会使用 SourceConstantAlpha=48；实际分层窗口命中中该边界值不可靠，仍可能被当作透明。
method: 新增 HiddenModeHitTestAlpha=64；隐藏反色后只在可见按钮圆角 tile 内把全透明像素补为预乘黑色 Alpha=64，叠加 SourceConstantAlpha=48 后仍约为 12/255，提升 User32 分层窗口命中可靠性。
保持按钮间隙、圆角外部、隐藏按钮和 FPS 信息区域透明穿透；已有非零 Alpha 像素不改动。
更新操作面板自测，要求透明交互像素等于 HiddenModeHitTestAlpha，并验证与隐藏态整体透明度叠加后仍至少为 1；同步版本、接口索引和性能文档。
reason: Alpha=1 属于过低边界值，无法覆盖用户真实桌面中的分层窗口命中行为；提高到 64 是在视觉仍较淡的前提下换取可靠点击。

scope: Codex Radar
module: Model IQ刷新、更新状态与额度缓存
diagnosis: CodexRadar 常规调度仍按北京时间每日窗口设计：当天模型数据未出现时会 10 分钟轮询，失败 2 分钟重试；这不匹配网站当前 am/pm 批次和用户期望的整点检查。
下方已更新/时间使用五阶段连接诊断 CheckedAtUtc，而不是 IQ 环实际成功更新的时间；失败或不完整请求还会把 ModelIqRefreshedAtLocal 改成当前时间。
current.json 的 Model IQ date 已出现 2026-06-16-am/pm 格式，原 DateTime 解析无法识别批次，不能按北京时间 0 点和 12 点两个基准判断新鲜度。
本地 quota.ini 不存在且运行时只依赖 session 扫描；内存 session 快照在 watcher 漏事件时可能长期相信旧 rollout 文件，导致额度环显示旧值或空环。
method: 新增北京时间下一个整点和当前半日窗口工具；CodexRadar 成功请求后排到下一个北京时间整点，网站未出新批次不再追加 10 分钟检查，失败、超时、不可达或不可用改为 10 分钟重试；Claude 失败重试仍保持 2 分钟。
CodexRadarSnapshot 增加 ModelIqDataWindowStartHourLocal/ModelIqDataWindowKnown，解析 current.json 的 yyyy-MM-dd-am/pm 并在缓存中写入 DataWindowHour；历史样本以半日窗口为 key，避免同一天 am/pm 互相覆盖。
连接流程下方文字改为读取 IQ 环最近一次成功更新到快照的时间，按北京时间 0 点/12 点基准显示 已更新/HH:mm 或 未更新/HH:mm；失败和 Incomplete 请求不再覆盖成功更新时间。
启动时先读 quota.ini；成功从 ~/.codex/sessions 读取额度后写回 quota.ini；复用内存 session 快照前每 30 秒确认是否有更新的 rollout 文件，watcher 事件会立即清空该确认缓存。

scope: 连接检测窗口
diagnosis: 右上角网络环境检测三枚状态框在隐藏反色防烧屏启用后，框底和图标内部的半透明装饰填充会参与后续位图反色，在高透明隐藏状态下视觉上变成亮色背景块。

scope: 网络监控窗口
diagnosis: 用户反馈 GFW 在肯定无丢包或明显小于 2% 的环境下仍显示不可判定。
复查发现 TryBuildGfwLocalNetworkGate 直接消费 LocalLoss、WanLoss、BaiduLoss 以及延迟/抖动类诊断；其中 LocalLoss 来源于默认网关滚动窗口，而 PingRollingSnapshot.LossPercent 显示的是当前活动公网/百度目标组丢包。
因此网关侧 ICMP 单独丢包、滚动延迟/抖动，或上一轮已确认丢包尚未恢复时的 0%/1.7% 活动目标丢包，都可能把 GFW 临时门控成不可判定。
method: TryBuildGfwLocalNetworkGate 增加门控边界：只有 WanLoss、BaiduLoss 或 LocalLoss 诊断同时满足 rollingLossConfirmed=true 且当前活动目标 rolling.LossPercent >= 2.0% 时，才返回 GFW 本地链路门控。
延迟、抖动、ICMP 被禁用、采样中、网关侧 ICMP 单独丢包以及当前活动目标低于 2% 的丢包，都不再让 GFW 显示不可判定；这些状态仍继续显示在 PING 行。
RunRollingPingSelfTest 新增 local-only loss=0%、local latency、未确认 WAN loss、确认 WAN loss 和 LocalLoss+活动目标 10% 丢包的门控断言。
同步刷新规则、网络架构、运行文档、功能索引、接口索引和版本号到 1.0.3.28。

scope: 修复 EvenRow 底部信息栏文字浮空（未在横线与底边间上下居中）与长文本截断
diagnosis: 用户反馈 EvenRow 底部栏（RC/DS/LLM/SF）文字浮空、未对横线与底边上下居中，且长文本（如 DS:¥473.36 低谷）显示不全被截断。
浮空根因：分隔横线画在 dividerY+S(1)-3.0，而底部信息面板顶从 dividerY+S(3) 起、底到 bounds.Bottom-S(2)，两者不一致且底部留 S(2) 空隙，导致文字在不匹配的区间内居中、整体偏上浮空。

method: 统一分隔线 Y：DrawEvenRowCompactDivider 改为在传入 y 精确绘制（去掉内部 +S(1)-3.0 偏移）；调用方以同一 dividerLineY 画线，并把底部信息矩形设为 RectangleF.FromLTRB(left, dividerLineY, right, bounds.Bottom)，配合 DrawEvenRowStatusText 的 LineAlignment.Center，使文字恰好在横线与底边之间上下居中。
重写 DrawEvenRowBottomInfoPanel：改用一个共享字号 GetEvenRowBottomInfoSharedFont，从基准字号逐步降到低下限（6.0*scale），选出让四项测量总宽 <= 可用宽度*0.99 的最大字号，再按测量宽度加均摊余量铺满整行；因此每项都拿到 >= 自身测量宽度的矩形，长文本不再截断。

scope: EvenRow 空余管理：圆环上移居中、左右间距收紧至约5px、宽窄自适应不重叠
diagnosis: 用户反馈 EvenRow 圆环上部空余太大、左右间距过宽，要求圆环在文字与顶部之间居中、元素间距收紧到最少5px，并要求在元素互相影响时解耦图层、既不影响也不重叠。
原因一：GetEvenRowCompactRingCellRect 把紧凑格下移对齐整格圆环位置，导致圆环偏低、上方留大空隙。
原因二：圆环尺寸由 min(cellWidth*0.86, heightArea) 决定，高度受限时列宽的 0.86 余量变成每个圆环两侧约19px的横向空隙；加权列又强制铺满整宽，使圆环间和状态列都很空。
method: 圆环竖直居中：GetEvenRowCompactRingCellRect 去掉旧的整格对齐下移，改为按 (下方到标签字形的间距 - 上方间距)/2 计算一个小幅下移（上限 S(10)），使圆环在紧凑格顶部与标签字形之间视觉居中。
解耦圆环尺寸与列宽（用户所说的不同图层）：新增实例字段 evenLayoutRingFillFactor，GetEvenLayoutCellRects 用它替代硬编码 0.86。EvenGrid 仍用默认 0.86，不受影响。
EvenRow 改为显式紧凑排布替代加权铺满：圆环直径由紧凑格高度推导；圆环列宽取 min(直径+S(10), 可用宽/5)，fill 因子设为 直径/(直径+S(10)) —— 宽窗口时圆环达到高度上限并保持约5px间距，窄窗口时圆环按比例缩小以容纳雷达与状态列、绝不重叠或溢出。
状态列按内容测量宽度（GetEvenRowStatusDesiredWidth），不再吞掉多余宽度；整行按 sideMargin 居中，多余宽度化为两侧等边距而非中间大空隙。
渲染自检增强（test-only）：RenderVariantSamples 注入真实长度 DeepSeek 余额并额外输出窄宽 codexradar-evenrow-narrow.png，用于复现并核对窄窗口不重叠。

移除 Claude 专用显示快照分支；GatherQuotaDisplayState 在 CLAUDE 模式下同样消费共享 quotaSnapshot，只保留 Claude 可用性判断。
防止 Claude 缓存把 ChatGPT/CODEX 服务健康误判为正常：UpdateCodexServiceHealth 与 UpdateServiceConnectivityHealth 只在 CODEX 有额度来源时使用 quotaSourceKnown。

scope: CodexRadar/ClaudeRadar EvenRow text-overflow fix and render-harness true-size correction
window_scope: CodexRadar EvenRow; standalone Claude Radar EvenRow; formal ARM64 runtime
module: Core.CodexRadarForm; Core.CodexRadarForm.EvenRow; Core.CodexRadarForm.RenderSample; Core.ClaudeRadarForm; Docs; Deployment
diagnosis: User reported both the CodexRadar and Claude Radar EvenRow windows looked wrong on the real 2880x1800 desktop ("比例和之前的完全不相符"), even though a fresh --render-codexradar/--render-clauderadar PNG looked clean.

Root cause: CodexRadarForm.RenderSample.cs and ClaudeRadarForm.cs RenderVariantSamples() rendered the sample canvas at settings.CodexRadarWidth/ClaudeRadarWidth * 2 while keeping form.scale = 2.0f, but the real running window sets this.Size = new Size(currentSettings.CodexRadarWidth, currentSettings.CodexRadarHeight) directly with no additional DPI multiplication (confirmed by GetWindowRect with SetThreadDpiAwarenessContext(PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) on the live process: the real window is exactly 580x120 physical pixels, matching settings.ini, not 1160x240). The harness canvas was therefore twice as wide as any real window, silently hiding genuine overflow.

At the true 580x116 size, CodexRadarForm EvenRow ring reset-date labels ("13:00", "07/04") ellipsis-truncated to "13..."/"07..." because DrawCodexRadarFittedText's shared 8.0*scale minimum font floor was too high for the narrow real ring-cell width.

ClaudeRadarForm EvenRow was worse: DrawClaudeRadarFittedText was missing StringFormatFlags.NoWrap, so text that still did not fit at the minimum size wrapped onto a second line and got clipped (e.g. "20:30" -> "20:3"/"0") instead of ellipsis-trimming on one line; separately, its shrink loop compared measured width against rect.Width + S(1) (a ~2px tolerance) while the actual DrawString call trims with zero tolerance, so the loop could stop believing it "fit" while the draw call still truncated (e.g. "省时" -> "省...").

Verified live: captured the actual running formal window pixels via PrintWindow (PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) at its real HWND rect, which matched the user's screenshot and the corrected render pixel-for-pixel before/after the fix.
method: Added an overload DrawCodexRadarFittedText(..., float minSizeUnits) that lets a caller lower the shrink-to-fit floor below the shared 8.0f default; used it (minSizeUnits=6.0f) only at the quota-cell reset-date label call site in DrawEvenLayoutQuotaCell, leaving all ~20 other call sites (Classic layout, EvenGrid rating/update text, etc.) on the unchanged default floor.

Added StringFormatFlags.NoWrap to ClaudeRadarForm.DrawClaudeRadarFittedText, matching CodexRadarForm's equivalent, so text that cannot fit even at the minimum size ellipsis-trims on one line instead of wrapping and clipping a second line.

Removed the "+ S(1)" slack from DrawClaudeRadarFittedText's shrink-loop fit check so it matches the zero-tolerance behavior of the actual DrawString/EllipsisCharacter call - the loop now only stops once the text truly fits, or the floor is reached.

Fixed CodexRadarForm.RenderSample.cs and ClaudeRadarForm.cs RenderVariantSamples() to size the render canvas at settings.CodexRadarWidth/ClaudeRadarWidth directly (no `* 2`) while keeping scale=2.0f, so future --render-codexradar/--render-clauderadar output matches the real physical window size instead of a canvas twice as wide.

Verified with a temporary diagnostic build (not shipped) that computed the exact real-size layout numbers (ringCellWidth, statusWidth, etc.) and traced the ClaudeRadarForm shrink loop iteration-by-iteration to confirm the +S(1) tolerance mismatch before writing the fix; removed all temporary diagnostic code/CLI flags afterward.
Bumped version, rebuilt ARM64, backed up both formal executable mirrors (D: and E:), overwrote both, restarted, and re-verified via PrintWindow capture of the live restarted process.
reason: The user could see genuine text truncation on their real 2880x1800 screen that the existing render-harness verification method could not catch, because the harness itself rendered at 2x the real window size. Fixing only the visible symptom without fixing the harness would have left the same blind spot for future layout work on either window.

After the fix, the same 580x116 true-size render showed "13:00", "07/04", "省时", "高效", "20:30", "07/08", "增智" all fully legible with no truncation.

scope: Codex Radar 5h/weekly quota counter zero-drop repair
window_scope: Codex Radar quota rings and quota decision diagnostics
diagnosis: quota-decision-history showed the 5h balance dropped from 100 to 0 at 2026-07-07 00:00:25+09:00 while network-check-history reported codex_provider_usage success; the value recovered to 95 at 00:08:27.
Local .codex session rate_limits for the same period showed primary used_percent progressing from 0 to 5, so the real remaining balance should have been about 100 to 95 rather than 0.

The provider parser multiplied all used_percent/used_percentage values <= 1.0 by 100. That is valid for utilization ratios but wrong for fields explicitly named used_percent or used_percentage; provider value 1 was treated as 100 percent used.
The same field-unit bug could also affect the weekly ring because both 5h and weekly provider slots used the same parser.
method: Changed provider usage parsing so used_percent and used_percentage are interpreted as percentage units, while utilization 0..1 remains the only ratio field that is multiplied by 100.

Moved provider snapshot memory/cache writes behind UI-thread validation; suspicious single-sample provider snapshots that collapse a high 5h or weekly balance to 0 without a material reset-time advance are rejected before updating memory or quota.ini.
Added quota snapshot source and used-field diagnostics, and extended quota-decision-history rows with source_kind, source used field name, raw used value and normalized used percent.
Added --test coverage for provider percent parsing, utilization parsing and zero-drop guard boundaries.
reason: Prevent a transient or differently-unitized provider response from emptying the 5h/weekly quota rings and corrupting quota.ini, while leaving enough diagnostics to prove which upstream field caused a future decision.

scope: NetworkMonitor RowPlan layout refactor spec for a downstream executor AI
window_scope: Documentation only; no runtime change
diagnosis: User reported overlapping elements in the network window and problematic IPv6 display. Code audit confirmed four concrete overlap mechanisms: fixed 7-row layout with S(12) min row height overflows the 112px minimum window height; DrawDnsAlertOverlay intentionally paints over long GFW text (1.0.4.16 residual risk); DrawHeader squeezes the alert text with non-shrinking DrawFixedText between status and public-IP segments; IPv4/IPv6/public-IP compaction uses fixed character counts (15/24/16) instead of pixel measurement, and an empty IPv6 row still occupies a full row.
method: Wrote an implementation spec proposing a plan-then-draw RowPlan layout engine: per-frame row plan with conditional row visibility (IPv6 hidden when no global/ULA address, WIFI hidden on wired), priority-based row degradation instead of sub-readable font shrinking, a measured right-side attachment slot unifying cloud tiles and the DNS alert strip (geometrically disjoint from GFW text), pixel-measured middle-ellipsis IP compaction replacing character-count magic numbers, a measurement-driven header, programmatic rectangle-disjointness self-test assertions, four new deterministic render fixtures, and a strict acceptance gate including a user sign-off step for the GFW/DNS-alert behavior change.
reason: User asked for a layout optimization proposal only; execution is delegated to another AI.

scope: Pixel-exact reproduction of the user-approved grouped-card mockup, measured from a real reference screenshot
window_scope: Network monitor Classic layout; formal ARM64 runtime
diagnosis: User was angry that the previous grouped-card deploy (1.0.4.31-1.0.4.33) still visually diverged from the approved mockup and demanded a pixel-exact rebuild ('元素大小和位置一个像素都不能差, 窗口固定628x250'). A prior offer to eyeball-compare was rejected; the user provided a real reference screenshot file (C:\Users\GengH\OneDrive\Desktop\..., 1108x464 PNG, noting the outer window border may not be fully captured) instead of accepting another visual approximation.
method: Measured the reference screenshot programmatically with Python/PIL/numpy: row/column projection profiles against the background color to find card fill/border boundaries; a higher-threshold text-vs-card-fill mask to isolate per-line text bands (avoiding the card border color contaminating the boundary); color-run segmentation (green/red saturated pixels vs background) to find each health-card chip's dot position, dot diameter, dot-to-text gap and chip-to-chip gap.

Converted every measured reference pixel coordinate to a fraction of the reference axis size (x/1108, y/464 with a small vertical margin-compression shift to absorb the acknowledged crop uncertainty at top/bottom), yielding the GroupedCardLayout static class: ~30 named float constants (HeaderTop/Bottom, TitleLeft/Right, StatusLeft/Right, TilesLeft/Right, Row1Top/Bottom, AddressLeft/Right, LinkLeft/Right, HealthTop/Bottom, per-card header/line Top/Bottom bands, AddrValueColLeft, LinkTextLeft, ChipRowTop/Bottom, ChipDotDiameter, ChipDotTextGapW, ChipGap) that reproduce the reference exactly when multiplied by this.Width/this.Height at 628x250.

Rewrote DrawContentClassic/DrawGroupedHeader/DrawAddressCard/DrawLinkCard/DrawHealthCard to compute every rect from these literal fractions instead of the previous proportional heuristics (content.Width*0.56 etc.); removed ComputeGroupedCardRects, DrawCardHeaderLabel, DrawCardLine, and the now-dead CombineNameAndType in favor of direct fraction-based RectangleF construction and a new DrawTextLine helper.

Matched reference content details found during measurement: address/link labels are IPv4/IPv6 (not IP4/IP6); link card line 1 is two-tone (bold interface name + muted type on the same row, type omitted when redundant with the name) instead of a single '·'-joined string; link line 3 shows a single representative rate value and auth algorithm only (no cipher suffix), matching the reference's simplified content.

Fixed a real font-rendering artifact discovered during verification: an odd fractional pixel size (8.5f) under GDI+ bold synthesis produced an uneven glyph gap for certain letter pairs (e.g. 'W' followed by 'PA3' rendered as 'W PA3'); rounding the value font size to a whole pixel eliminated it.

Fixed a real regression introduced mid-implementation: the health-card clip/wrap region was first set to only the single reference-measured chip-row height, silently hiding an entire wrapped second row in the 5-bad-DNS-server stress fixture; corrected to clip against the card's own full remaining interior (chip-row-top to the card's own bottom edge) so a wrapped row displays fully inside the card border, while an even more extreme overflow still clips invisibly at the card's exact boundary rather than bleeding past it.
reason: Deliver literal pixel-for-pixel fidelity to the user-approved reference image instead of another approximate reproduction, using programmatic measurement in place of visual estimation.

scope: Settings window color theme now matches the Classic floating-window scheme (black + red/yellow/green) instead of the unused WarmCard OLED amber palette
window_scope: Settings window (Win11SettingsForm); no floating-window runtime change
diagnosis: User described their actual floating windows as black background with red/yellow/green (plus light-red/light-green) as the only status/selection colors, and pointed out the settings window is gold instead. Investigation confirmed: DesignTokens.SettingsWarmTheme's header comment explicitly stated it was designed to match the WarmCard OLED restyle scheme (warm-gray fills + OledAmber accent). Checked the real settings.ini on this machine: every window (MainWidget, NetworkMonitor, PowerThermal, ConnectionCheck, Operation) has RenderVariant=Classic; none use WarmCard/AmberHud/Typographic/Phosphor. So the settings theme was deliberately matched to a variant nobody actually runs, while the real Classic scheme (Colors.AppBackground near-black + Colors.Success/Warning/Danger) was never reflected in Settings.
method: Redefined every color in DesignTokens.SettingsWarmTheme (the single source all 15 Win11SettingsForm color fields and ~8 direct call sites already read from) instead of touching Win11SettingsForm.cs: WindowBase now aliases Colors.AppBackground (18,19,22) exactly; TextPrimary/TextSecondary/TextMuted alias Colors.TextStrong/TextMuted/GlyphMuted; Accent aliases Colors.Success (green, the widgets' 'healthy/active' hue) with AccentHover/AccentPressed computed as a 15% white / 20% black blend of Success; ErrorText aliases Colors.Danger (red). Neutral card/divider/toggle/button fills were recomputed as opaque pre-blended equivalents of the same white-alpha-over-AppBackground overlay the layered windows already use for their own card fills (DesignTokens.White(10)/White(28) etc.), using the identical blend formula, rather than picking new warm-brown hex values.

No other file needed changes: Win11SettingsForm.cs's 15 static Color fields and all in-place DesignTokens.SettingsWarmTheme.* call sites (toggle switch, close-button hover, nav item, command buttons) already route through this single class, confirmed zero direct OledAmber/NeonGeek/hardcoded hex leaks remain outside it.

Updated Docs/Component-Refresh-Rules.md's settings visual-resources row, which had explicitly documented the (now corrected) WarmCard-matching rationale, to state the real Classic-matching rationale and note the settings.ini evidence that no window actually runs an OLED variant.
reason: Make the settings window's color language consistent with the actual on-screen floating widgets instead of an OLED restyle variant nobody has selected.

scope: Restore an independent, real-time OpenAI status probe for the CodexRadar EvenRow API summary
window_scope: Codex Radar EvenRow API summary and R/O/C/D LED column
diagnosis: 1.0.4.19 (Spec T3 dead-path removal) deleted the old five-stage connection diagnostics, which was the only caller of the status.openai.com and chatgpt.com probes; that deletion was correct at the time because that whole path was dead.

However the API summary's OpenAI item was left wired to codexServiceHealth, which UpdateCodexServiceHealth(bool quotaKnown) derived from whether the local Codex quota read succeeded, not from OpenAI's actual service status.

User explicitly requested that the OpenAI item reflect real service availability so it can be checked before actually using Codex/OpenAI, matching how the Claude item already works (an independent TryReadClaudeStatus/RefreshClaudeStatusIfNeeded probe against status.claude.com).
method: Added OpenAiStatusUrl/OpenAiStatusTimeoutMs constants and openAiServiceHealth/openAiStatusLock/nextOpenAiStatusRefreshUtc/openAiStatusRequestRunning/openAiStatusRefreshTrigger fields, mirroring the existing Claude fields exactly.

Added TryReadOpenAiStatus(WidgetSettings) which performs a real HTTPS GET against status.openai.com/api/v2/summary.json (Statuspage v2 schema) through AiRequestProtection, and RefreshOpenAiStatusIfNeeded() which schedules it (15 min interval when Normal, 2 min retry otherwise), byte-for-byte structured like TryReadClaudeStatus/RefreshClaudeStatusIfNeeded.

Wired RefreshOpenAiStatusIfNeeded into the main tick loop next to RefreshClaudeStatusIfNeeded, plus ForceRefresh, PrimeCodexWebRefreshSchedule and ResetServiceHealthAfterTestMode refresh-nudge points.
Renamed the shared refresh-interval helper GetClaudeRefreshInterval to GetServiceStatusRefreshInterval since it is now used by both probes.
Deleted UpdateCodexServiceHealth(bool quotaKnown) and its call site in ApplyCodexQuotaSnapshot; codexServiceHealth is no longer derived from Codex quota-read success.

Renamed the codexServiceHealth field to openAiServiceHealth and updated UpdateServiceConnectivityHealth/ApplyServiceHealthTestMode/ResetServiceHealthAfterTestMode to treat it like radarServiceHealth/claudeServiceHealth (Offline on no network, reset to Unknown afterward so the live probe repopulates it) instead of inferring it from quota reads.

Added SetOpenAiServiceHealth mirroring SetClaudeServiceHealth, and replaced the special-cased AddOpenAiServiceAlertCandidate with a direct AddServiceHealthAlertCandidate(candidates, "openai", "OpenAI", openAiHealth, openAiChecking) call so OpenAI now goes through the same generic alert path as Radar/Claude.

Renamed the dead CodexRadarRandomTestSnapshot.CodexHealth field to OpenAiHealth and actually wired it into the random-test alert branch, fixing a pre-existing gap where random test mode never varied the OpenAI LED.

Restored the external_api.openai.status INTERFACE_INDEX.jsonl entry from removed to active with the new entrypoint/behavior, split the old bundled codex_radar.openai_component_health FEATURE_INDEX.jsonl entry so it now only covers the still-removed chatgpt.com probe, and added a new codex_radar.openai_status_probe feature entry; updated Docs/CodexRadar-Architecture.md section 7 to describe the restored independent probe instead of the quota-based fallback.
reason: User wants to know whether OpenAI/Codex is actually usable before attempting to use it, which requires a genuine live status probe rather than inferring availability from whether a prior quota read happened to succeed.

scope: Redesign the operation panel RadialDial variant into a tiered category menu with a custom icon set, category color coding, and a redesigned core button
window_scope: Operation panel RadialDial render variant only; other five render variants and the flat-grid Classic path are untouched
diagnosis: The first RadialDial cut (1.0.4.57) shipped a flat two-ring layout of 17 leaf actions that reused the flat grid Draw*Glyph icon methods and a plain flat-color core circle with three dots.

User feedback rejected all three choices: icons must be drawn fresh for this variant, the menu needed a hierarchical/tiered structure (example given: clicking Settings should reveal 程序设置/特殊设置/系统设置), categories should carry distinct background colors, and the core button needed a full visual redesign.

The window remains anchored bottom-left (PositionOperationWindow) so any redesign still has to fit inside the same 8-82 degree up-right quadrant; a tiered design needed per-level geometry rather than a single fixed set of 17 rects.
method: Replaced the flat RadialItemId two-ring model with a RadialLevel state machine (Collapsed -> Root -> Category -> SubCategory): Root shows five category nodes (Settings/Power/SystemTools/Battery-conditional/Assist), clicking one drills into Category showing 2-4 children, and the one Settings child SpecialSettingsBranch (特殊设置) drills one level further into SubCategory showing LinkBlockToggle/QuotaPlanToggle/CtfRestart (the former AiQuickMenuForm popup contents).

Collapsed a two-ring geometry engine into a single adaptive ring reused at every level via ComputeRadialLayout()/ComputeRingRadius()/ComputeArcOffsets(), sized to whatever the current level shows so the window naturally shrinks as navigation drills deeper.

Authored ~24 new hand-drawn glyph methods (DrawHexNutGlyph, DrawPowerRingGlyph, DrawWrenchGlyph, DrawBatterySparkGlyph, DrawSparkleGlyph, DrawAppWindowGlyph, DrawTileGridGlyph, DrawBeakerGlyph, DrawGaugeGlyph, DrawRestartLoopGlyph, DrawDockChevronGlyph, DrawBarsGlyph, DrawTogglesGlyph, DrawRefreshLoopGlyph, DrawBatteryPauseGlyph, DrawBatteryCheckGlyph, DrawCaptionBubbleGlyph, DrawHalfMoonGlyph, DrawChainLinkGlyph, DrawPieWedgeGlyph, DrawKeyboardGlyph) that do not call any flat-grid Draw*Glyph method.

Added GetCategoryColor/GetLeafColor/MutedCategoryTint to give each category (and the special-settings advanced branch) a distinct muted fill color carried from its root node into its children circles and into the core gradient while that category is active.

Redesigned DrawRadialCore with a diagonal two-stop gradient fill, a soft PathGradientBrush glow, and a double-ring border, replacing the flat single-tone disc; the core icon itself switches between a four-point spark (Collapsed/Root) and a back chevron (Category/SubCategory), doubling as the back-navigation control.
Added a thin outer expand-ring visual cue on every category node and on the SpecialSettingsBranch leaf to signal it expands further.

Rewrote HandleRadialMouseUp/NavigateRadialBack/CollapseRadialFully to route clicks by current level instead of a flat index, while leaf actions still dispatch through the existing single-purpose methods (ExecuteButton, PulseSeelenDockFromOperationPanel, ExecuteRestartButtonDoubleClick, ExecuteAppSettingsButtonDoubleClick, setAiBlockAction/setQuotaPlanAction, RunElevatedCtfmonRestartHelper) with no duplicated business logic.
Updated RunRadialDialSelfTest to assert Root/Category/SubCategory layouts, the three-child Settings branch, the three-leaf special-settings branch, and 90-degree quadrant containment at every level.

scope: Codex Radar quota ring provider spike source isolation and weekly consumption baseline repair
window_scope: Codex Radar quota rings; quota decision history diagnostics
diagnosis: Root cause was not the draw layer, CodexRadar public site, or old quota.ini cache. quota-decision-history showed chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage returned a successful transient provider sample at 2026-07-08T03:52:40Z with five_hour=99 and weekly=100 after the previous accepted weekly balance was 13.

The same pattern reappeared after the first 1.0.4.60 deployment at 2026-07-08T04:09:24Z: session/provider had just shown weekly=12, then provider returned five_hour=99, weekly=100 and a later five-hour reset, and three seconds later provider returned five_hour=79, weekly=12 and the older reset again.

UpdateQuotaReadDeltaTracking treated any five-hour balance increase as fiveHourWindowAdvanced even when the old reset time was still hours in the future; line logic then copied the transient weekly=100 into weeklyQuotaAtFiveHourWindowStartPercent. Later duplicate samples kept weekly_consumption_baseline_percent=100, so the visible weekly consumption tail looked like it started from 100.

The original 1.0.4.60 weekly spike guard was insufficient because it only checked weekly reset material advance and did not reject a provider sample whose old reset boundary had not yet reached its due time.
method: Added provider five-hour early reset spike rejection: a near-full five-hour provider sample is ignored if the previous five-hour reset is still outside the due grace window and the incoming reset jumps forward.
Strengthened provider weekly spike rejection: a low-to-full weekly jump is ignored when the old weekly reset is not due yet, even if the incoming sample claims a later reset boundary.
Narrowed fiveHourWindowAdvanced so a known reset boundary must be due and moved; balance increase alone is only a fallback when no reset boundary is available.
Added stuck weekly baseline repair: a 95+ weekly baseline with stable low weekly data is reset to the current weekly balance and logged as suspicious_weekly_consumption_baseline_repaired.
Added self-test coverage for the observed 79->99/12->100 early-reset spike and for stuck 100 weekly baseline repair.
Updated architecture, refresh rules, feature index, interface index and version metadata to 1.0.4.61.
reason: Prevent a transient successful ChatGPT usage provider sample from poisoning the five-hour/weekly consumption baselines and make the already-polluted weekly baseline self-heal on the next stable low balance.

scope: Rebuild the operation panel RadialDial variant on a generic multi-level tree so drilling into a category no longer hides the rings above it, plus same-level rails, a selected-path connector line, toggle red/green coloring, an idle auto-collapse timer, and a re-capped 1/3/5/7 category tree
window_scope: Operation panel RadialDial render variant only; other five render variants and the flat-grid Classic path are untouched
diagnosis: The prior RadialDial redesign (1.0.4.58/59) still replaced the visible ring whenever a category was drilled into, so the root ring disappeared once you opened Settings; the user rejected this via a napkin sketch showing all levels staying visible simultaneously with gray same-level rails and a highlighted selected path.

The tree of categories/leaves was hard-coded as C# enums switched over in several places (GetRootCategories/GetCategoryChildren/GetCategoryColor/draw-dispatch/tooltip-dispatch), which the user flagged as hard to extend -- adding one button meant touching five different switch statements.

Toggle-type leaves (link block/quota plan/hover opacity) used the same muted category tint as every other leaf, giving no visual signal of their on/off state; the user asked for green/red fill by state.
The user asked for the menu to auto-collapse after sitting idle for a while, which the old design did not need (levels self-collapsed on navigation) but the new always-visible-levels design does.
The user asked for a stricter, more compact category cap (level1<=3, level2<=5, level3<=7) than the prior 5-category root, to keep every ring tight regardless of how many actions exist.
method: Replaced the RadialLevel/RadialCategoryId/RadialItemId enum-and-switch model with a generic RadialNode tree (Id/Label/BaseColor/DrawIcon delegate/Children/Execute/GetToggleState/IsUnavailable/IsBusy/GetTooltip) built once in BuildRadialRoots(); adding a button or a new nesting level now only means adding a node there, not touching geometry, hit-testing, drawing, or click-dispatch code.

Re-categorized the tree into 3 root categories (Settings/System/Assist) capped at 5 level-2 children each and 7 level-3 children for the two branches that go a level deeper (Settings > SpecialSettings, System > Power), replacing the previous flat 5-category root.

Replaced the id-free navigation state with radialMenuOpen + radialSelectionPathIds (a list of node ids, not node references); ResolveSelectionPath() re-resolves the chain against the live tree on every use and silently truncates a stale id (e.g. after battery buttons disappear) instead of holding a dangling reference.

ComputeRadialLayout() now computes and returns every level from the root ring down to the end of the current selection path in one pass, and DrawOperationWindowRadialDial() draws every one of those rings every frame, so opening a deeper level no longer hides the rings above it.

Added DrawRadialSameLevelRail (gray polyline connecting siblings within one ring) and DrawRadialPathConnectors (light-green polyline from the core through every selected node down the active path), both drawn under the node circles.

Reworked node fill precedence in DrawRadialNode to: unavailable (gray) > busy (amber) > toggle-type leaf colored green (on) / red (off) via DesignTokens.Colors.Success/Danger > selected branch node (blue ring + light-blue fill) > plain muted category tint.

Redesigned the core to show the active root category icon (once one is selected) plus small progress dots along its bottom edge indicating how many rings are currently open, replacing the old fixed spark/back-chevron-only core.

Added TickRadialIdleCollapse/ShouldRadialIdleCollapse and hooked it into OperationForm.ProcessSharedInteractionTick (the shared per-tick hook other windows already use) so the whole menu auto-collapses after ~3 seconds without interaction, since levels no longer self-collapse while browsing.

Rewrote RunRadialDialSelfTest to assert the 3/5/7 tree caps, that multiple rings stay simultaneously visible at each drill depth, that a stale selection id truncates safely, and the idle-collapse threshold condition.

scope: Replace foreground-window visibility polling with Seelen-style application window state tracking
window_scope: All monitoring floating windows
diagnosis: VisibilityMode=HideWhenFullscreen used NativeMethods.IsForegroundWindowFullscreen, which only inspected GetForegroundWindow and raw screen coverage, so ordinary maximized/borderless states could be conflated and all monitor windows shared one global hidden flag.
AutoHoverOpacityMaximizedEnabled used a 750 ms foreground-window polling cache instead of the same application-window state model used for fullscreen visibility.
The requested Seelen UI approach requires persistent application window state, event-driven updates, and a fullscreen test that separates thick-frame maximized windows from true fullscreen windows.
method: Added ApplicationWindowStateTracker, backed by NativeMethods.WindowEventHook, to cache interactable top-level application windows and refresh the cache on foreground/create/destroy/show/hide/state/location/name/parent/cloak events plus each main control tick.

Extended NativeMethods.ApplicationWindowInfo and TryGetApplicationWindowInfo to expose bounds, screen bounds, minimized, maximized and fullscreen flags while filtering self, SeelenUI, shell/desktop, tool, untitled and unstable frame windows.
Replaced WidgetForm HideWhenFullscreen with per-form, per-screen decisions using the tracker top-window fullscreen state, so child windows no longer inherit one global foreground-window result.
Replaced the old maximized auto-hide foreground polling cache with the same window-state tracker and deleted NativeMethods.IsForegroundWindowFullscreen/IsForegroundWindowMaximizedOrFullscreen.
Updated settings help text, runtime documentation, feature index and interface index for the new visibility implementation.
reason: Implement the user-requested Seelen UI style window-state recognition and remove the old foreground polling visibility code.
verification_evidence: ARM64 candidate build completed successfully at _build/visibility-state/DesktopCodexAssistant-arm64-test.exe.
--test-settings-bindings, --test-layout, --test and --test-logger all returned exit code 0.
residual_risks: The implementation uses WinEvent plus main-tick revalidation rather than a dedicated shell-hook HSHELL_FULLSCREEN_ENTER/EXIT window; the geometry/style check is still the authority for fullscreen state.

A maximized background window can still trigger AutoHoverOpacityMaximizedEnabled because the setting text describes any non-self/non-Seelen maximized or fullscreen application window, not only the foreground app.

scope: Expand Seelen-style visibility behavior to five user-selectable tiers
window_scope: All monitoring floating windows
module: Settings.WidgetSettings; Settings.Win11SettingsForm; Core.WidgetForm; Core.ApplicationWindowStateTracker; Interop.NativeMethods; Docs.Indexes; Docs.Interfaces
diagnosis: The previous setting surface did not expose the requested visibility tiers, and the old implementation only had a fullscreen-oriented behavior path.
The user required five tiers: always visible, hidden when fullscreen, hidden when maximized, hidden when overlapped, and desktop-only; hidden when maximized must also include fullscreen.

The implementation must follow the Seelen UI approach already introduced in 1.0.4.65: event-updated application-window state cache, IsZoomed maximized state, WS_THICKFRAME exclusion for ordinary maximized windows, and rectangle-based monitor decisions.
method: Expanded WidgetVisibilityMode to AlwaysVisible, HideWhenFullscreen, HideWhenMaximized, HideWhenOverlapped and DesktopOnly, and changed normalized/default visibility to HideWhenFullscreen.
Updated settings UI enum labels and VisibilityMode help text to show the five Chinese labels and the maximized-includes-fullscreen rule.
Moved WidgetForm visibility decisions through ShouldHideFormForVisibilityMode and ApplyChildWindowsVisibilityMode so main and child monitor windows are evaluated per form and per monitor.

Added ApplicationWindowStateTracker.ShouldHideForVisibilityMode: AlwaysVisible/DesktopOnly return false, HideWhenFullscreen uses the top same-screen fullscreen app, HideWhenMaximized uses any same-screen maximized or fullscreen app, and HideWhenOverlapped uses same-screen rectangle intersection.
Exposed NativeMethods.IsApplicationWindowFullscreenForState for self-tests so WS_THICKFRAME maximized windows are verified not to count as fullscreen while borderless screen-covering windows do.

Connected ApplicationWindowStateTracker.RunSelfTest to --test-layout and covered all five visibility tiers, monitor-boundary behavior, empty window lists, maximized-includes-fullscreen, and overlap geometry.
Updated runtime documentation, feature index, and interface index to describe five-tier visibility rather than the old fullscreen-only path.
reason: Implement the user-requested five-tier visibility model using the Seelen-style application window state tracker and remove the old fullscreen-only behavior surface.

scope: Show Windows global Energy Saver state in the power/battery panel and automatic Windows power-mode mapping
window_scope: PowerThermal window battery module and WidgetForm WindowsPowerMode refresh
diagnosis: The power panel only displayed the normalized base power mode from AC/DC overlay, Win32_PowerPlan or powercfg, so a Windows global Energy Saver toggle could still show plain 平衡.
The app also lacked GUID_POWER_SAVING_STATUS subscriptions, so WindowsPowerMode scheduling could miss an immediate global Energy Saver change if the effective-power-mode callback did not fire.
The existing --render-powerthermal sample used only the base PowerThermalHeight, which hid the auto-down battery module and could not validate this visual change.
method: Added NativeMethods.GUID_POWER_SAVING_STATUS and registered it in both WidgetForm and PowerThermalForm.
PowerThermalForm now reads Windows.System.Power.PowerManager.EnergySaverStatus into PowerReading.EnergySaverKnown/EnergySaverEnabled and includes those fields in display equality checks.
